summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with worsening groin pain following a recent hospitalization for a multidrug-resistant UTI. He was found to have candiduria and bilateral inguinal intertrigo, both contributing to his discomfort. He was treated with a 14-day course of oral fluconazole for the fungal urinary infection and miconazole powder for the skin infection, with significant improvement. His chronic indwelling catheter was replaced, and he continued a 10-day course of piperacillin-tazobactam for a prior bacterial UTI. His other conditions, including diastolic heart failure, benign prostatic hypertrophy, type 2 diabetes, and a stable right renal mass, remained unchanged. He was discharged to extended care with instructions to complete his antifungal and antibiotic regimens and follow up for liver function testing and urology surveillance.
